strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly articulates exploratory causal inference and the need to discover unknown treatment effects in RCTs without a priori hypotheses

Novel theoretical insight: Theorems 3.1–3.2 elegantly formalize the 'Paradox of Exploratory Causal Inference' showing standard tests reject all entangled neurons as power increases; Figure 3 provides clear empirical demonstration
Creative methodological solution: NES's recursive stratification is principled and well-motivated; Theorem 4.1 provides consistency guarantees; simple, implementable algorithm with provided code

Comprehensive semi-synthetic experiments: controlled evaluation on CelebA with known ground truth across sample size and effect magnitude; extensive ablations (testing procedures, AIPW vs AD, zero-effect); NES clearly outperforms baselines in precision-recall trade-offs

Strong presentation and reproducibility: well-written with clear motivation, effective figures, organized exposition; code and detailed experimental protocols provided; uses publicly available datasets
weaknesses: Strong unverifiable assumptions: Assumptions A.1–A.3 are critical but difficult to verify in practice. A.1 (FM sufficiency) is strong; A.2 (Alignment/Principal-Max) is restrictive; A.3 (ε-leakage bound) provides no practical verification method. Theorem 4.1 depends entirely on these, limiting practical applicability

Fundamental SAE identifiability unresolved: authors acknowledge recent work (Heap et al. 2025; Leask et al. 2025) shows SAEs produce 'post-hoc artifacts'; paper concludes method should serve only 'as a rescue system for hypotheses that may have been missed'—severely limiting scientific applicability and undermining claims about discovering 'ground truth' effects

Weak real-world validation: only one real-world experiment (ISTAnt, n=44 videos) with r=2 effects. Effect 1 (grooming) was already known from prior work. Effect 2 (background) is acknowledged as likely an artifact of experimental design bias, not a true causal effect. No follow-up experiments validating discovered effects prospectively

Limited experimental scope: semi-synthetic uses only r=2 effects with no scaling analysis for r>>2. Missing crucial comparison to Causal Feature Learning (Chalupka et al. 2017)—the most directly related baseline—despite discussion. Baselines limited to simple methods (t-test, FDR, Bonferroni); no comparison to causal discovery or CATE methods

Theory-practice gap: Algorithm 2 doesn't explicitly verify Assumptions A.1–A.3 or adapt based on them. Critical parameter choices lack guidance: how to select λ (sparsity), α (significance level), ε? For ISTAnt, Bonferroni correction is dropped without justification, weakening statistical guarantees

Evaluation metric circularity: ground truth neurons in semi-synthetic experiments identified by F1-scores on the same SAE codes that NES discovers, partially validating that NES finds what the SAE encodes rather than independent scientific truth

Missing ablations and analysis: no investigation of scaling to large r, effect magnitude heterogeneity, or poor-quality SAE representations. Foundation model selection role not analyzed. SAE hyperparameter sensitivity (beyond λ) not studied. Limited discussion of failure modes

strengths: Novel problem formulation distinguishing rationalist and empiricist approaches to causal inference in RCTs with unknown outcomes
Elegant theoretical characterization of the 'Paradox of Exploratory Causal Inference' showing standard multiple testing fails under entanglement (Theorems 3.1-3.2)
Principled algorithm (NES) with recursive stratification and asymptotic consistency guarantees (Theorem 4.1)
Comprehensive semi-synthetic evaluation with known ground truth showing NES outperforms baselines as power increases
Strong reproducibility effort with detailed experimental protocols, promised code, and minimal Python implementation
weaknesses: Single real-world experiment (n=44) with questionable findings: one expected effect (grooming) and one acknowledged finite-sample artifact (background color); insufficient to validate practical utility
Critical assumptions largely unvalidated empirically: FM sufficiency, SAE monosemanticity, identifiability, and principal margin condition all asserted without empirical verification on real data

Authors explicitly acknowledge identifiability is 'strongest assumption' and poorly understood; further state method should only serve as 'rescue system for hypotheses missed'—severely undermining claims of discovering novel effects
Experimental scope limited to r=2 effects; scalability to larger effect spaces unknown; only binary outcomes supported; no guidance on hyperparameter selection
Method's core depends on SAE quality yet SAEs have known interpretability issues (spurious features, Heap et al. 2025); the background color artifact in real experiment exemplifies this problem
Semi-synthetic experiments use unrealistic entanglement patterns; limited comparison to other exploratory methods beyond classical hypothesis testing; no sensitivity analysis to assumption violations
Gap between theory (asymptotic guarantees) and practice (finite samples, unverified ε-leakage bounds, no finite-sample theory provided)

strengths: Clear and timely problem formulation distinguishing rationalist vs. empiricist approaches to causal inference in modern scientific discovery
Elegant theoretical contribution: Theorems 3.1–3.2 formally characterize the 'Paradox of Exploratory Causal Inference,' showing how standard multiplicity corrections fail under effect entanglement
Principled algorithmic solution with theoretical guarantees: NES's recursive stratification strategy is intuitive and Theorem 4.1 provides consistency under reasonable assumptions
Comprehensive experimental validation including semi-synthetic benchmarks with ground truth, extensive ablations, and reproducibility artifacts (code, implementation details, public datasets)
Well-executed presentation with clear motivation, intuitive explanations of technical concepts, and good use of figures to illustrate key ideas
weaknesses: Strong and inadequately validated assumptions: Assumptions A.1–A.3 (sufficiency, alignment, bounded leakage) are critical yet lack empirical validation. No guidance on when they hold or robustness to violations; ε (leakage bound) is unknown in practice

Severely limited real-world validation: only one trial (ISTAnt, n=44) discovering 2 effects (one being an experimental artifact); insufficient to support claims about practical scientific discovery. Multiple diverse real-world applications needed

Unresolved SAE identifiability concerns: paper acknowledges recent negative results on SAE reliability yet proposes using the method merely as 'rescue system for missed hypotheses'—this conservative framing contradicts the exploratory discovery aspiration

Incomplete practical guidance: no principled methods for selecting significance level α (especially for small samples like n=44), leakage threshold ε, or which testing rule to use; ablations show testing choice significantly impacts results
Circular evaluation on semi-synthetic data: ground truth constructed using SAE F1-scores assumes monosemanticity, then NES is validated against this same assumption

Limited scope and novelty: experiments cover only r≤2 effects; primary technical contribution (recursive stratification) is incremental, combining established FM+SAE+stratification techniques; the 'paradox' is somewhat intuitive given entanglement
Missing efficiency and power analysis: no sample size comparisons vs. pre-specified hypotheses, no power calculations, no guidance on when NES is preferable
Insufficient treatment of foundation model bias: acknowledges FM bias as a concern but provides limited empirical assessment of how this affects discovery

strengths: Novel theoretical contribution: Theorems 3.1-3.2 rigorously characterize the 'Paradox of Exploratory Causal Inference,' showing standard multiple testing becomes increasingly liberal under neural entanglement
Elegant methodological solution: NES's recursive stratification is intuitive and simple to implement, with consistency guarantees provided by Theorem 4.1

Comprehensive semi-synthetic validation: Extensive experiments across varying sample sizes, effect sizes, encoders, SAE dimensions, and non-linearities consistently demonstrate NES maintains precision while baselines collapse
Rigorous theoretical framework: Clear distinction between rationalist and empiricist approaches; detailed proofs in appendix with explicit assumptions

Honest limitations discussion: Authors properly acknowledge strong assumptions, SAE identifiability concerns, and position method as supplementary rather than replacement for hypothesis-driven approaches
weaknesses: Extremely strong and often unverifiable assumptions: Assumption A.1 (sufficiency), A.2 (principal alignment), and A.3 (arm-wise decomposition with bounded transport error) are difficult to verify in practice without knowing ground truth. Method violates A.2 under jump-ReLU, failing completely (Figure 24), suggesting brittleness

Critically weak real-world validation: Single experiment with n=44 ants; one discovered effect is an experimental artifact (background marking bias); the other (grooming) was already known from prior rationalist analysis, so NES discovered no new effects

Unresolved SAE identifiability and interpretability concerns: Recent work (Heap et al. 2025, Leask et al. 2025, Wu et al. 2025) shows SAEs can produce spurious interpretability. Method critically depends on monosemanticity, yet this is difficult to achieve and impossible to verify in advance

Insufficient practical guidance: No guidance on verifying assumptions, choosing ε threshold, or setting α when sample size is small. Real experiment abandoned Bonferroni correction due to small sample size (n=44), invalidating theoretical guarantees

Multiple testing issues in practice: With m=4608 codes and n=44, Bonferroni cutoff becomes prohibitively stringent (α/m ≈ 0.00001). Asymptotic theory may not apply with small samples. Trade-offs between Type I and Type II error not thoroughly analyzed

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the tension between hypothesis-driven and data-driven scientific discovery
Clear formalization and proof of the 'Paradox of Exploratory Causal Inference' showing failure of standard multiple testing under entanglement
Clever recursive stratification approach for handling effect entanglement across high-dimensional SAE representations
Rigorous theoretical analysis with detailed proofs and consistency guarantees (Theorem 4.1)
Extensive experimental validation including semi-synthetic benchmarks with controlled ground truth and numerous ablations
Reproducible work with public code snippets, public datasets, and detailed experimental protocols
weaknesses: Core theoretical assumptions (Sufficiency, Alignment, ε-Leakage) are strong and largely untestable in practice, undermining the practical applicability of theoretical guarantees

Foundation method (SAEs) has well-documented interpretability problems (spurious structures on random networks, failure to isolate atomic concepts) that fundamentally compromise using SAEs for scientific causal discovery
Weak real-world validation: only one trial (n=44), method didn't discover unknown effects (grooming was already known from prior work), and identified experimental confounds rather than new science
Circular validation problem: claims to achieve unsupervised effect discovery but requires domain experts to interpret and filter results, unclear advantage over supervised causal inference baselines
Foundation model bias acknowledged as problematic for scientific conclusions but not addressed; no methodology provided to verify FM adequacy for a given domain

Method still returns statistically significant spurious correlations (e.g., background marking confound in real trial) requiring expert dismissal, demonstrating it doesn't solve the core false discovery problem
Limited scope: only handles binary treatments and outcomes, assumes data sufficiency (all outcome information in X), and requires SUTVA
Incomplete comparison to alternatives: no comparison to semi-parametric efficiency bounds, Bayesian variable selection, or recent causal discovery methods
Real-world result undermines main claims: neuron 550 (background artifact) returned as significant, requiring expert filtering—this is a failure of the method presented as evidence of robustness

strengths: Novel problem formulation distinguishing rationalist vs. empiricist causal inference with clear motivation (Matthew effect)
Clear characterization of 'Paradox of Exploratory Causal Inference' (Theorems 3.1-3.2): as power increases, all entangled neurons become significant regardless of correction
Principled algorithmic solution (NES) with formal consistency guarantees (Theorem 4.1) via recursive stratification
Comprehensive experimental validation: semi-synthetic experiments with ground truth, extensive ablations, multiple baselines, real-world application
Technically rigorous: explicit assumptions, detailed proofs, reproducibility emphasis with code snippets
Well-presented with clear motivation, effective figures, and logical progression from problem to solution
weaknesses: Strong untestable assumptions (A.1-A.3): sufficiency of FM, principal alignment, and ε-leakage bounds cannot be verified without ground truth, limiting practical applicability
Heavy dependence on SAE reliability during period of SAE skepticism: recent work documents spurious interpretability and failures to isolate concepts; no guarantee assumptions hold outside CelebA
Minimal real-world validation: only one experiment (n=44 ISTAnt videos) with mixed results (one true effect, one design confound; F1=0.398 suggests incomplete capture)
Identifiability gap: paper adopts empirical stance toward SAEs without assuming identifiability, yet Theorem 4.1 requires strong alignment assumptions—this disconnect unresolved
Practical guidance insufficient: no principled way to set ε, verify Γ>2ε, or determine when to stop recursion; arm-wise residualization improves performance but marked optional
Gap between theory and positioning: method framed as exploratory discovery but ethics statement recommends using as 'rescue system for missed hypotheses,' which is weaker claim
